name: Portland Museum of Art
funding: $13.4M expenses (2024); FY2024-25 donors, Osher funds, NEA, Maine Arts Commission, KeyBank, L.L.Bean, Avangrid/CMP, Allagash.
watch: No adverse finding; roster not checked. Named: Avangrid Foundation with Central Maine Power, alcohol (Allagash). The 2024-25 fight over demolishing 142 Free St went to court and split the city.
records_note: Annual reports from 2013 to 2024-25 and audited statements are on its site; the 2024-25 report names donors and trustees.

name: Aldrich Contemporary Art Museum
funding: $3.3M expenses (2023); 2025 gifts from individuals, CT Office of the Arts, foundations, Bank of America, Fairfield County Bank, galleries.
watch: Fashion founding fortune; roster not checked. Named: Bank of America, Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation (Point72), alcohol (Freixenet Mionetto, Litchfield Distillery). No controversy found.
records_note: Annual reports from 2018 to 2025 are on its site, a named supporters list covers gifts received in 2025, and trustees are listed.

name: The Phillips Collection
funding: $16.6M expenses (2023); Phillips family endowment (steel and banking), private trustees.
watch: Altria (tobacco) has sponsored shows for 30+ years; Bloomberg has backed the gala ~20 years. No protest found. 2025 deaccession criticised.
why_flagged: Altria (tobacco) has sponsored shows for 30+ years; Bloomberg has backed the gala ~20 years. No protest found. 2025 deaccession criticised.
records_note: It posts annual reports, audits and Form 990s for 2014 to 2025, a donor and sponsor list in the 2025 report, and its trustees.

name: Parrish Art Museum
funding: $6.1M expenses (2023); Hamptons donors, Bank of America, J.P. Morgan Private Bank, Related, Suffolk County, NYSCA and IMLS.
watch: No adverse finding; roster not checked. Bloomberg Philanthropies is on the 2024 donor list ($20k-49k), a name under campaign. No protest at the museum found.
records_note: Annual reports 2017 to 2025 and audited statements are on its site, a named 2024 donor list is public, and trustees are listed.

name: Belarus Free Theatre
watch: Registered in England 22 May 2012 with its office at the Young Vic, London, and operations in Poland. Trustees per Companies House: Michael Attenborough, Mark Ball, Baroness Helena Kennedy, David Lan, Jude Law, Dame Maria Miller, Alison Stanley, Laura Wade, Samuel West. Producer of 'Official. Unofficial. Belarus' in Venice 2026.
records_note: Companies House holds its full accounts for years to January 2020 to 2025 and its site names eleven trustees; no annual report or funder list.

name: Francis Skaryna Belarusian Library and Museum
watch: Founded 1971 at 37 Holden Road, North Finchley; the largest Belarusian collection in western Europe; governed by a board of trustees; dormant and deregistered 2011, revived 2014 and re-registered 27 Apr 2015.
records_note: Annual reports for 2020, 2024 and 2025 are on its site, accounts are with the Charity Commission, trustees are listed, and no donors are named.

name: Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation
funding: State foundation set up in 2017; runs the 2025 Bukhara Biennial.
watch: Bukhara Oil (Uzbekneftegaz refinery) is a partner; ACWA Power funded a prize show with Saudi Diriyah Biennale Foundation. Critics call it image-building.
why_flagged: Bukhara Oil (Uzbekneftegaz refinery) is a partner; ACWA Power funded a prize show with Saudi Diriyah Biennale Foundation. Critics call it image-building.
records_note: A state-run foundation under the Presidential Administration; its site names only its chairperson and posts no reports, accounts or donors.

name: Fundación Oswaldo Vigas
funding: Artist-estate non-profit founded 2010; no funding sources disclosed.
records_note: Its site has a staff page naming a chairman, custodian and director, but no board, reports, accounts or funders.

name: Fundación Sala Mendoza
funding: Founded 1956 by the Mendoza industrial family; partly self-funded through bookstore and art sales.
records_note: Its La Sala page names a president and general manager but no board; there are no reports, accounts or sponsor lists.

name: Nguyen Art Foundation
funding: Founded 2018, privately funded by Quynh Nguyen, founder of flavour and fragrance firm Viet Huong JSC and co-founder of the EMASI schools. It works from its own financial resources.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, donor list or board found; the team page names the founder, director, manager and curator only.

name: The Factory Contemporary Arts Centre
funding: Founded 2016; self-funded social enterprise where art sales and an on-site cafe pay for programmes.
records_note: The live site returns an empty page; archived copies show no reports, accounts, donor list or board, only a founder and former curatorial staff.

name: Livingstone Office for Contemporary Arts (LoCA)
funding: Artist-founded non-profit (2014); Perennial partners include Zeitz MOCAA and the National Arts Council Zambia.
watch: Launched the Mosi-oa-Tunya Perennial in Sept 2026; funder roster not public.
records_note: Its Our Sponsors page names 15 partners, undated; a team page lists 13 people, but there is no board, report or accounts.
